items.s: I have two ___.
items.tip: Most words add -s for more than one: one cat → two cats.
items.say: I have two cats.
items.ask: I have two blank.

items.s: There are three ___ on the table.
items.tip: Words ending in -x, -s, -sh or -ch add -es: box → boxes.
items.say: There are three boxes on the table.
items.ask: There are three blank on the table.

items.s: The two ___ are sleeping.
items.tip: Consonant + y: change y to i and add -es: baby → babies.
items.say: The two babies are sleeping.
items.ask: The two blank are sleeping.

items.s: Five ___ are playing in the park.
items.tip: child is special: one child → two children.
items.say: Five children are playing in the park.
items.ask: Five blank are playing in the park.

items.s: I can see four ___ in the sky.
items.tip: Add -s for more than one: star → stars.
items.say: I can see four stars in the sky.
items.ask: I can see four blank in the sky.

items.s: I brush my ___ every morning.
items.tip: tooth is special: one tooth → two teeth.
items.say: I brush my teeth every morning.
items.ask: I brush my blank every morning.

items.s: Look at those little ___!
items.tip: mouse is special: one mouse → two mice.
items.say: Look at those little mice!
items.ask: Look at those little blank!

items.s: We picked lots of ___ from the tree.
items.tip: Consonant + y: change y to i and add -es: cherry → cherries.
items.say: We picked lots of cherries from the tree.
items.ask: We picked lots of blank from the tree.

items.s: My brother is ___ than me.
items.tip: To compare two things, add -er and use than: tall → taller than.
items.say: My brother is taller than me.
items.ask: My brother is blank than me.

items.s: Grandpa is the ___ person in my family.
items.tip: the + -est means number one of a group: old → the oldest.
items.say: Grandpa is the oldest person in my family.
items.ask: Grandpa is the blank person in my family.

items.s: A cheetah is ___ than a horse.
items.tip: Two animals compared, so -er + than: fast → faster than.
items.say: A cheetah is faster than a horse.
items.ask: A cheetah is blank than a horse.

items.s: My cat is ___ than my dog.
items.tip: Comparing two pets: small → smaller than.
items.say: My cat is smaller than my dog.
items.ask: My cat is blank than my dog.

items.s: Winter is ___ than summer.
items.tip: -er + than compares two things: cold → colder than.
items.say: Winter is colder than summer.
items.ask: Winter is blank than summer.

items.s: The giraffe has the ___ neck of all the animals.
items.tip: the … of all = number one, so -est: long → the longest.
items.say: The giraffe has the longest neck of all the animals.
items.ask: The giraffe has the blank neck of all the animals.

items.s: This bag is ___ than that one.
items.tip: Comparing two bags: light → lighter than.
items.say: This bag is lighter than that one.
items.ask: This bag is blank than that one.

items.s: My teacher is the ___ person I know.
items.tip: the + -est = the most of all: kind → the kindest.
items.say: My teacher is the kindest person I know.
items.ask: My teacher is the blank person I know.

items.s: My mum is a ___. She teaches children.
items.tip: Add -er to a doing word to name the person: teach → teacher.
items.say: My mum is a teacher. She teaches children.
items.ask: My mum is a blank. She teaches children.

items.s: The ___ has lots of cows and pigs.
items.tip: A person who works on a farm is a farmer (farm + -er).
items.say: The farmer has lots of cows and pigs.
items.ask: The blank has lots of cows and pigs.

items.s: Lily sings very well. She is a great ___.
items.tip: A person who sings is a singer (sing + -er).
items.say: Lily sings very well. She is a great singer.
items.ask: Lily sings very well. She is a great blank.

items.s: Tom is a football ___.
items.tip: A person who plays a sport is a player (play + -er).
items.say: Tom is a football player.
items.ask: Tom is a football blank.

items.s: The ___ painted a picture of the sea.
items.tip: A person who paints is a painter (paint + -er).
items.say: The painter painted a picture of the sea.
items.ask: The blank painted a picture of the sea.

items.s: I am a good ___. I love books!
items.tip: A person who reads is a reader (read + -er).
items.say: I am a good reader. I love books!
items.ask: I am a good blank. I love books!

items.s: The ___ swims very fast.
items.tip: swim ends in one vowel + one consonant, so double the m: swim → swimmer.
items.say: The swimmer swims very fast.
items.ask: The blank swims very fast.

items.s: The ___ drives the bus to school.
items.tip: drive already ends in e, so just add -r: drive → driver.
items.say: The driver drives the bus to school.
items.ask: The blank drives the bus to school.
